judgements.justification: Neither area chair set the outcome from their own reading: A's adopted Reviewer_x5V9's critique to settle a 2-2 split, and B's leaned on a 7.0 mean that includes an 8 from the most careful reviewer.
No recommendation rested on impact beyond the paper's setting; B's praise of a GF-to-GD bridge describes the paper's own contribution.
After near-identical restructuring promises, four of B's five reviewers raised (4TKP 6 to 8, kYKg 6 to 7, r4iB, DACB), while A's detractors x5V9 and jeQC kept 4 and 3.
Thin reviews sit on both sides (A: Reviewer_4GXj; B: Reviewer_hENG), and B's Reviewer_4TKP wrote the most careful review on either side, so scrutiny is not lopsided overall.

Only A raised the positioning critique (generic tool versus deep-linear guarantee, no evidence trajectory comparison is not less efficient) and the eps-shrinking step size against Arora et al.; A's area chair cited the positioning critique.

Both committees named the dense main text, the linear-only guarantee and the step size exponentially small in depth; A held them against the paper, B accepted promises to fix them and gave a spotlight.
Reviewer_nsKx agreed with x5V9 on presentation after discussion but no score change is recorded; every recorded move followed the authors' response.
No rating contradicts its own text: r4iB's 6 matches 'not surprising', the 7s from hENG and DACB carry stated low confidence rather than contrary text.
B's unsure reviewers gave 7s, not borderline scores, so they lifted rather than held B's mean at the threshold.
A's area chair followed x5V9, but A split 2-2 at equal confidence, so x5V9 was not an outlying reviewer.
The score gap grew mainly through B's post-rebuttal raises, not from similar verdicts placed at different scale points.
B's area chair cited reviewer agreement, but Reviewer_4TKP rated 8 above the accept level and A's mean (5.0) was lower, not similar or higher.

Reviewer_4TKP raised 6 to 8 because 'the proposed changes completely address my concerns', and DACB raised on the same restructuring promise; A's x5V9 saw 'little guarantee that the weaknesses will be fixed'.

B's three-sentence meta-review says all reviewers saw 'a strong contribution' and omits the density, scope, linear-only and tiny step-size weaknesses its reviewers named; A's meta-review carried its reviewers' weaknesses forward.

B's Reviewer_kYKg called the paper the first convergence proof of a fixed-size deep network, which overstates it (the paper's own Section 7 lists earlier deep-linear GD guarantees), and that novelty claim fed kYKg's 7.
The authors told B's Reviewer_4TKP that the step-size bound 'goes below 1e-20' and that no tightness experiments were run, and 4TKP then raised 6 to 8.
A's objections were answered: jeQC's 2021-08-24 comment drew an author reply on 2021-08-25, and x5V9's update repeated earlier points.
The final scores differ (mean 5.0 split 2-2 versus 7.0 within one point), so the tier split is not a cut-off difference on near-identical scores.
B's area chair did not follow a less-informed majority against its best reviewer: 4TKP, the most specific reviewer, rated 8; A's reviewers all sat at confidence 3.
Both committees raised the same kind of presentation and scope concerns and received the same promises; the difference was in trusting them, not in what a response could fix.
Neither committee has an outlying score; A is a 2-2 split and B lies within one point of 7.0.
Reviewer_4GXj never replied after the rebuttal, but A's 2-2 split makes 4GXj no outlier, and the silent reviewer sat on the accept side.
Neither area chair set aside a detractor as unreliable; A followed its detractors and B had none below 6.
B's reviewers called the scope too large for a conference, but that did not lower B, which gave a spotlight; A never raised venue fit.

B's meta-review says 'All the reviewers agree that the manuscript is a strong contribution', overstating r4iB's 6 ('not surprising', techniques 'not new') and DACB's 7 ('unable to evaluate correctness').
Three of A's four reviewers engaged after the rebuttal (x5V9 and nsKx updates, jeQC's comment); only 4GXj stayed silent.

added.name: Non-expert reviewers' accept scores counted in full
added.definition: Reviewers on one committee who said they could not verify the main results (proofs unread, area unfamiliar) still gave clear accept scores, and the area chair counted them at full weight, which lifted that committee's mean and tier above what its checked assessments supported.
added.justification: R09 covers unsure reviewers who gave borderline scores that held a mean down; here unsure reviewers gave accept scores that lifted the mean, and R04 does not fit because B also had the most careful review on either side.

added.name: Area chair settled an even split for one side
added.definition: One committee's reviewers split evenly between accept and reject at similar confidence, and the area chair settled the split by adopting one side's critique without addressing the other side's scores, so the recommendation reflected that side alone while the other committee had no such split.
added.justification: R10 requires the followed reviewer to be an outlier and R01 requires the area chair's own reading; here the area chair broke a 2-2 tie at equal confidence by taking the reject side's argument.

reasoning: Both committees saw the same narrow but new result and the same weaknesses (dense text, linear-only guarantee, tiny step size), so R06 applies. The gap opened at the rebuttal: B's reviewers credited promised restructuring and raised (R03, R13), even after the authors conceded a step-size bound below 1e-20 (R16), while A's detractors discounted the same promises. Only A raised the positioning and Arora et al. comparisons (R05). B's meta-review dropped its reviewers' weaknesses and overstated their agreement (R14, R25), and kYKg's 7 rested on an overstated novelty claim (R15). Two causes had no existing reason: B's spotlight counted two accept scores from reviewers who said they could not verify the results (R27), and A's area chair broke an even 2-2 split by adopting the reject side's critique (R28).
